FLYW should remain in the universe as an education payments infrastructure candidate, but later layers must isolate education vertical revenue, international-student sensitivity, and payment-rail dependency.

node: Student-loan servicing, education payments, communications, and compliance systems
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-company universe around regulated servicing infrastructure, education payments, borrower communications, collections workflows, and compliance-heavy operating systems. The strongest direct public-market mappings are Nelnet for student-loan servicing plus education payments, Flywire for education payment infrastructure, Maximus for outsourced federal student-loan servicing operations, and Navient as a speculative shadow candidate because it retains student-loan assets and historical servicing/compliance exposure but has materially reduced or exited direct federal servicing exposure. This pass intentionally emphasizes underfollowed infrastructure and regulated workflow providers rather than obvious schools or edtech brands.
